en.title: Number of Unused Skills in a Query Time Window
en.description:
Each log entry has a skill ID and a request time. For each query q, count the skills that have no request in the closed interval [q−window,q], and output the answers in the original query order.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains numSkills m q window; each of the next m lines contains a 1-based skill ID and a time, and the last line contains q query times. The four size/window parameters are in 1..100000, times and queries are in 1..100000, and IDs are valid.
en.output: Output q idle skill counts in the original query order.
en.explanation: Example 1: in the window 5..10 the active skills are 1 and 2, so 1 is idle; in 6..11 only skill 2 is active, so 2 are idle. Example 2: in the original query order the active counts are 3, 1, 1, so the idle counts are 3, 5, 5. Example 3: query 6 includes the request at the left end 5, so 0 are idle; query 7 does not, so 1 is idle.
hints: Sort the logs by time and the queries by time as well. Use two pointers to maintain the logs inside the window, record a frequency per skill and keep the number of active skills; answer=(total skills)−(active count).
